problem: Perception-based humanoid loco-manipulation needs paired tuples of egocentric images, language instructions and robot-compatible whole-body kinematics. No existing source provides this at scale. Teleoperation is expensive. Human mocap has no robot egocentric view. Egocentric video has no robot kinematics.
motivation: Two technologies are now mature enough to be connected. 3D Gaussian Splatting gives photorealistic, metric-scale Real2Sim scene assets, and sim-trained whole-body trackers (BeyondMimic/SceneBot) give Sim2Real execution of kinematic references. The missing link is a data generator that pairs rendered egocentric views with G1 kinematic behaviours. Generating behaviour with privileged scene information (object poses, walkable regions) and rendering observations afterwards (hindsight rendering) removes the need for human demonstrations.
key_idea: Synthesize G1 navigation and box-interaction trajectories with scene-conditioned diffusion models inside 3DGS-reconstructed real rooms, render matching egocentric RGB afterwards, and fine-tune π0.5 into a Vision-Language-Kinematics policy whose 1 s whole-body kinematic chunks (plus wrist-contact labels) are executed by a contact-aware RL tracker on the real Unitree G1.
insight: Most of the sim-to-real work is split between (a) predicting kinematics rather than torques, so a blind, separately trained tracker absorbs the dynamics gap, and (b) visual domain randomization. Removing randomization drops walking success in the perturbed lab sim from 90% to 41%. Lighting randomization alone recovers most of it (87%), while camera randomization alone gives only 48%. The ablations also show: predicted wrist-contact labels are essential, since Pick (Floor) without contact labels gets 0/5 real-world trials in both scenes; navigation is learned with little data, whereas contact-rich manipulation scales with data volume (Pick (Surface) goes from 0% at 10% data to 46% with full data). Surface-level pick/put remains weakest (e.g., 8/20 real Put (Surface) in the lab), which the authors attribute to limited support-surface-height coverage in the retargeted OMOMO interaction data.
method: Real2Sim scene assets: iPhone 14 Pro Polycam scans (RGB + LiDAR) reconstructed as metric-scale 3DGS. 4 furniture layouts × 2 environments (lab, apartment). A viser-based tool is used to hand-annotate oriented semantic 3D boxes and walkable-floor polygons on an extracted point cloud.

Task/waypoint/language generation: sample target objects, collision-free initial poses (with a visibility check for walk-to), sparse waypoints, and surface-height-dependent wrist contact frames and relative wrist poses. Instructions come from templates (e.g., 'walk toward the chair', 'place the box on the table'). 12 modes: 6 evaluated (Walk To, Turn Around, Pick/Put Floor, Pick/Put Surface) plus auxiliary random walk/turn/carry modes.

G1 motion synthesis: CHOIS/HIHI-style conditional transformer diffusion adapted to the G1 representation [global joint positions, 6D rotations, sin/cos joint angles] with a differentiable G1 forward-kinematics loss. The navigation model is trained on BONES-SEED G1 motions. The interaction model is trained on OMOMO retargeted via OmniRetarget and conditions on object BPS geometry, initial object state, desired wrist poses and contact labels. Post-processing: foot-contact IK anti-sliding (HIHI) and EgoAllo-style wrist-pose matching. Trajectories with scene penetration are filtered.

Hindsight egocentric rendering: synthesized trajectories are replayed in Isaac Sim with the 3DGS scene and a virtual head-mounted ZED 2i calibrated to the real camera. Domain randomization covers camera extrinsics (±2 cm, ±3°), focal length (±2%), dome-light intensity/yaw, colour jitter, noise, blur, and synthetic motion blur.

VLK policy: π0.5 fully fine-tuned with the action head replaced by G1 kinematic states [heading-normalized Δx, Δy, Δψ, root height, 6D root orientation, sin/cos q, L/R wrist-contact bits]. Given the current RGB image, instruction and state, it predicts H=30 frames (1 s at 30 Hz). Training uses x0-prediction flow matching plus auxiliary losses: focal foot-contact loss, accumulated-root drift, FK ankle/wrist, and foot-skating.

Execution: a blind contact-aware RL whole-body tracker (SceneBot-based, trained in IsaacLab) runs at 50 Hz. It converts references (lower-body joints, head/wrist 6D poses, root pose, contact labels) into joint PD targets and activates contact-aware wrist behaviour when contact is on.

Deployment: Triton-optimized real-time VLA server on an RTX 5090 (31 ms inference, ~63 ms end-to-end replan, ~1.8 Hz replanning). Ψ0-style real-time chunking with a 10-frame overlap. Sharpness-based frame selection (max variance of Laplacian over a 0.3 s buffer) counters motion blur.

setting.backbone: π0.5 VLA (fully fine-tuned) as the high-level VLK policy + SceneBot-based contact-aware RL whole-body tracker (trained in IsaacLab); CHOIS-style diffusion models for data synthesis
setting.training_data: Fully synthetic: 1000 trajectories per layout per mode × 4 layouts × 12 modes = 48,000 trajectories per environment (lab and apartment); generated in ~600 GPU-hours, with no human demonstrations. 10% held out for validation. The motion generators are trained on BONES-SEED (G1 navigation motions) and OMOMO retargeted to G1 via OmniRetarget.
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB (ZED 2i left image 672×376 resized to 224×224) + language instruction + current G1 kinematic state (contact bits autoregressively predicted)
setting.action_space: 1 s chunks (30 frames @30 Hz) of G1 whole-body kinematic states + binary wrist-object contact labels, executed by an RL tracker outputting joint PD targets at 50 Hz
setting.simulator: Isaac Sim (3DGS rendering) + MuJoCo (closed-loop physics evaluation); tracker trained in IsaacLab
setting.privileged: none at inference (privileged object poses/walkable regions are used only for data generation). However, test environments are the same physical rooms that were scanned for training (layouts varied), and root pose comes from an onboard state estimator.

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark is used; all results are on the authors' own lab/apartment tasks. Results are reported as success counts (x/20 real-world, x/1000 simulation), and metric keys encode the denominator. Split labels are approximate: 'test' marks real-world trials, and 'val' marks the held-out 10% of synthesized sequences from the same layouts. The data-volume ablation is shown mainly in a figure, not reproduced here. The text quotes 46% full-data Pick (Surface), while Table 1 gives 458/1000. There are no external baselines; the comparisons are internal ablations only.
results: On the physical Unitree G1 (120 trials), navigation and floor-level box handling are near-perfect: Walk To 20/20 lab and 19/20 apartment, Put (Floor) 20/20 in both. Surface-level pick/put is much weaker (lab 11/20 and 8/20; apartment 13/20 and 15/20). Closed-loop MuJoCo simulation shows the same pattern (e.g., Walk To 994/1000 vs Pick (Surface) 458/1000 in the lab). Removing visual domain randomization cuts perturbed walking success from 90% to 41%, and removing contact labels yields 0/5 on real Pick (Floor). No external baseline is compared.
limitations: Interaction synthesis is bounded by OMOMO coverage (large objects only), so the system does bimanual box transport rather than small-object grasping. The contact-aware tracker does not support precise grasping.

Training and test use the same scanned physical environments (only layouts vary); scene annotation (3D boxes, walkable regions) is manual; language instructions are simple templates. Generalization to unseen buildings or free-form instructions is not evaluated.
No comparison against other methods (e.g., teleoperation-trained humanoid VLAs). Surface-height interactions remain unreliable.
